sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Scaling Factor
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a determinant as a 'scaling factor' for area/volume during a linear transformation. Prerequisite: Students should understand vectors as arrows and matrices as functions that move those arrows.
sections.example: Visualize a unit square with a cute cat icon inside. When the matrix transforms the space, the square stretches into a parallelogram. The determinant is the ratio of the new area to the original area.

sections.title: The 2x2 Case: Geometric Calculation
sections.content: Define the determinant for a 2x2 matrix using the cross-multiplication formula (ad-bc). Relate this directly to the area of a parallelogram spanned by two column vectors.
sections.example: Matrix [[a, b], [c, d]]. Show an animation where the vectors (a, c) and (b, d) form a parallelogram. The value 'ad-bc' represents the signed area.

sections.title: The Sign Significance: Orientation
sections.content: Explain that the sign of the determinant indicates orientation. A positive sign means the 'handedness' is preserved; a negative sign means the space has been flipped (mirrored).
sections.example: Show a robot character on a screen. If the determinant is negative, the robot appears in a mirror reflection, effectively swapping its left and right.

sections.title: Singularity: When the Area Collapses
sections.content: Discuss the special case where the determinant is zero. This happens when the transformation squashes the space into a line or a point, losing dimensionality.
sections.example: An animation of a 3D cube being flattened into a flat 2D 'pancake'. When the volume becomes zero, the information is lost, and the matrix is 'non-invertible'.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Synthesize the knowledge: Determinant measures scaling, indicates orientation, and identifies invertibility. Essential for solving systems of equations and computer graphics.
sections.example: A quick montage of a video game character changing size/perspective, controlled by determinant calculations in the engine's background math.

storyboard.title: Intuitive Hook: The Scaling Factor
lecture_lines: The determinant measures the scaling factor of space.
A transformation stretches or shrinks objects in space.
Original area relates to the new area.
animations: Highlight area doubling, color change to #00FFFF.

storyboard.title: The 2x2 Case: Geometric Calculation
lecture_lines: For 2x2 matrices, calculate ad minus bc.
This value defines the parallelogram's area.
Vectors span the transformed area in space.

storyboard.title: The Sign Significance: Orientation
lecture_lines: The sign shows the orientation of space.
Positive determinant means original orientation is preserved.
Negative means the space has been mirrored.

storyboard.title: Singularity: When the Area Collapses
lecture_lines: Zero determinant means the area collapses.
Transformation squashes dimensions, losing all information.

storyboard.title: Summary & Application
lecture_lines: Determinants measure scaling and reveal orientation.
They help identify invertible matrix transformations.
Essential for math and computer graphics.
